chapter_seo_title: The Three-Foot Sword's Final Stance: Ji Ning Ascends a New Realm in Desolate Era
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning comprehends the final 'Sword Tour of the Three Realms' stance and tempers it with a dragon's wisdom. He then re-evaluates just what it means to be 'comparable to a Celestial Immortal'.
og_title: The Ninth Sword of the Immortal Beixing!
og_description: After thirty years of silent cultivation, Ji Ning surpasses his legendary predecessor and looks toward the ultimate challenge of the Three Realms Palace.
twitter_title: The Sword is Mastered. The Next Trial Awaits.
twitter_description: Ji Ning finishes his epiphany, mastering the powerful 'Three-Foot Sword', and gets a harsh reality check on the true hierarchy of the Three Realms.

lore_anchors.definition: A legendary peerless Sword Immortal from the Grand Xia world’s history. Ji Ning’s mentor at the Black-White College left behind the famous *Three-Foot Sword* technique.

surfaces: Sword Tour of the Three Realms
lore_anchors.definition: The ninth and most powerful stance of the *Three-Foot Sword*. It manifests a black dragon phantom representing wild, unrestrained power.
A popular saying in the Xianxia world that means a cultivator's combat power is roughly on par with the *weakest* of Celestial Immortals, not the average or strongest.
The Fiendgod Body Refining stage equivalent to the Ki Refining Earth Immortal stage; a Fiendgod body refiner at this level possesses godlike regenerative powers.
An extremely advanced spatial movement technique that allows a cultivator to instantly travel across vast distances.
The top-secret, high-level vault within Mount Innerheart containing techniques powerful enough to dominate the Three Realms. The reward for a cultivator who has mastered the basics.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does ‘comparable to a Celestial Immortal’ really mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s a very vague term in Xianxia, usually meaning a cultivator is strong enough to fight the *weakest* or most average Celestial Immortal. It doesn’t mean they can beat a veteran or a genius immortal.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Ji Ning want to temper the Ninth Stance?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He believes it is too wild and unrestrained, which goes against the Daoist principle of ‘亢龙有悔’ — a successful dragon must know when to hold back to avoid disaster. He wants to make it more controlled and thus more effective.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Ji Ning’s strength level now?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has reached the fifteenth level of the Crimsonbright Diagram (comparable to a late-stage Fiendgod Body Refiner) and has fully mastered the Three-Foot Sword. He is considered nearly invincible against anyone below the Celestial Immortal level.
